newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh urged to prepare for 21st century.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh urged to prepare for 21st century.

text.p: Bangladesh must roughly double its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and industrial growth in the next eight years to meet the challenges of the next century, a business leader said on Thursday.

"To face challenges...the rate of GDP growth will have to be raised to 12 percent from 5.1 percent by year 2005. The contribution of industries in the GDP should be raised at 20 percent from the present 11.5 percent," Sharif Afzal Hossain, President of the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries, told a news conference.
Hossain said the government should invest 150 billion taka ($3.48 billion) to revamp ailing industries to boost their contribution to GDP.

"The process of globalisation (of trade and business) will be complete by year 2005. There will remain no hurdles in international trade, no tariff barriers in countries of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)," Hossain said.
"The whole world will become a single market. This will bring a great challenge for Bangladesh. To face the challenges we need to protect local industries."
Hossain urged politicians to protect economic activities from political unrest and called for a moratorium on trade union activities until 2005.
Infrastructure like power, gas, road, port facilities should be developed, he said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told a meeting of senior economists in Dhaka on Thursday she expected Bangladesh to attain a growth rate of up to eight percent by the turn of century.
This compares with a current 4.7 percent, officials said.
